headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared file-based workflows; Plane’s broad egress raises downstream exposure concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no shared channel by profile, but Plane accepts file uploads and handles notes/files, so if its output is copied into LlamaFactory prompts or training data, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks a documented isolation/provenance layer, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads are copied into LlamaFactory prompts or datasets without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF an operator manually bridges Plane notes/files into LlamaFactory input, prompt injection risk exists.
mitigations: Sanitize and strip instructions from uploaded files before reuse.
Use a fixed prompt template that quotes external text as data only.
Keep Plane exports and LlamaFactory inputs in separate folders.
Add a manual review step before any copy-paste bridge.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and roadmaps and has broad network egress; LlamaFactory is local-only with no egress and no filesystem read/write. If both are used on the same workspace, Plane can expose shared file contents to its backend, creating a realistic leakage path even though LlamaFactory itself is constrained.
conditions: IF Plane is given sensitive files from a shared workspace, those contents may leave the local environment.
IF LlamaFactory outputs are copied into Plane issues or notes, sensitive text can be retained in Plane.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in Plane uploads.
Use separate workspaces for Plane and LlamaFactory.
Redact secrets before uploading any file to Plane.
Disable broad egress at the network layer for Plane if feasible.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploaded attachments.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with Plane. Plane also lacks write_filesystem in the profile. With no overlapping write authority, only read-level or manual workflow overlap remains, which is low risk.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF a separate tool gives Plane git or filesystem write privileges, contention could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only on shared resources.
Assign distinct directories per agent.
Avoid letting either agent manage git state.
Use an external lock if a shared mutable resource is introduced.
requires-engineering: add resource-locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can store issues, tasks, and notes, so if LlamaFactory-generated text is imported into Plane without verification, Plane may treat it as authoritative work content. LlamaFactory has no built-in verification or downstream action controls in the profile, so the pair supports a plausible unverified handoff path.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory output is pasted into Plane issues or notes without review, errors can cascade.
IF Plane automations act on imported text, mistaken LlamaFactory content can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane issues from LlamaFactory output.
Mark LlamaFactory output as draft, not authoritative.
Cross-check facts against source documents before import.
Limit Plane automations on imported text.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for imported content.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source with docs-only evidence. The only compliance-relevant surface is Plane’s file uploads and broad egress, but without a stated regulated data class or policy mismatch, the pair shows only a documented-gap risk.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Plane and the deployment policy is stricter than LlamaFactory’s local use, compliance review is needed.
IF a jurisdictional residency rule applies to Plane-hosted data, mismatch risk may arise.
mitigations: Do not upload regulated data to Plane without policy review.
Keep regulated workflows local to LlamaFactory.
Document retention settings for Plane uploads.
Review residency requirements before enabling file uploads.
requires-engineering: configure tenant-specific retention controls.
